import requests, json
B="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data"
r=requests.get(f"{B}/molecule/CHEMBL1431.json",timeout=60).json()
print("PREF_NAME",r.get("pref_name"),"| max_phase",r.get("max_phase"),"| first_approval",r.get("first_approval"))
print("SMILES",r["molecule_structures"]["canonical_smiles"])
print("MW",r["molecule_properties"]["full_mwt"],"ALOGP",r["molecule_properties"]["alogp"])
print("INDICATION_CLASS",r.get("indication_class"))
m=requests.get(f"{B}/mechanism.json?molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL1431&limit=100",timeout=60).json()
print("N_MECH",m["page_meta"]["total_count"])
for x in m["mechanisms"]:
    print(" MECH:",x.get("mechanism_of_action"),"| action",x.get("action_type"),"| target",x.get("target_chembl_id"),"| direct",x.get("direct_interaction"),"| refs",len(x.get("mechanism_refs") or []))

import requests, collections
B="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data"
for t in ["CHEMBL2363065","CHEMBL3391681"]:
    d=requests.get(f"{B}/target/{t}.json",timeout=60).json()
    print(t, d.get("pref_name"), "|", d.get("target_type"), "|", d.get("organism"),
          "| comps:", [c.get("accession") for c in d.get("target_components",[])])
rows=[]
for mid in ["CHEMBL1431","CHEMBL1703"]:
    off=0
    while True:
        a=requests.get(f"{B}/activity.json?molecule_chembl_id={mid}&limit=1000&offset={off}",timeout=120).json()
        rows+=a["activities"]
        if not a["page_meta"]["next"]: break
        off+=1000
print("TOTAL activity rows:",len(rows))
print("assay types:",collections.Counter(r.get("assay_type") for r in rows))
print("top standard_types:",collections.Counter(r.get("standard_type") for r in rows).most_common(12))
pot=[r for r in rows if r.get("pchembl_value")]
print("rows with pChEMBL:",len(pot))
pot.sort(key=lambda r: -float(r["pchembl_value"]))
seen=set()
for r in pot[:25]:
    k=(r.get("target_chembl_id"),r.get("standard_type"))
    print(f"{r.get('target_pref_name')} ({r.get('target_chembl_id')}) {r.get('standard_type')}={r.get('standard_value')} {r.get('standard_units')} pChEMBL={r['pchembl_value']} org={r.get('target_organism')} assay={r.get('assay_chembl_id')}")

import requests, json, statistics
# --- Guide to PHARMACOLOGY ---
G="https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/services"
lig=requests.get(f"{G}/ligands",params={"name":"metformin"},timeout=60).json()
for l in lig:
    print("GtoPdb ligand:",l["ligandId"], l["name"], "| type",l.get("type"), "| approved",l.get("approved"))
lid=lig[0]["ligandId"]
inter=requests.get(f"{G}/ligands/{lid}/interactions",timeout=60).json()
print("GtoPdb interactions n=",len(inter))
for i in inter:
    tgt=requests.get(f"{G}/targets/{i['targetId']}",timeout=60).json()
    print("  ->",tgt.get("name"),"| affinity",i.get("affinity"),i.get("affinityType"),
          "| action",i.get("action"),"| type",i.get("type"),"| species",i.get("targetSpecies"),"| ref pmid",i.get("refs"))

import requests
q="""query D($id:String!){ drug(chemblId:$id){ id name drugType description isApproved: hasBeenWithdrawn
 maximumClinicalTrialPhase
 mechanismsOfAction{ rows{ mechanismOfAction actionType targetName targets{ id approvedSymbol approvedName } references{source ids} } }
 indications{ count rows{ disease{ id name } maxPhaseForIndication } } } }"""
r=requests.post("https://api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4/graphql",
                json={"query":q,"variables":{"id":"CHEMBL1431"}},timeout=60).json()
print(r.get("errors"))
d=(r.get("data") or {}).get("drug")
if d:
    print(d["id"], d["name"], d["drugType"], "maxPhase",d.get("maximumClinicalTrialPhase"))
    for m in d["mechanismsOfAction"]["rows"]:
        print(" MoA:",m["mechanismOfAction"],"|",m["actionType"],"| targetName",m.get("targetName"),
              "| targets",[(t["approvedSymbol"],t["id"]) for t in (m.get("targets") or [])],
              "| refs",m.get("references"))
    print(" indications count:",d["indications"]["count"])
    for i in d["indications"]["rows"][:15]:
        print("   -",i["disease"]["name"],i["disease"]["id"],"phase",i["maxPhaseForIndication"])

import requests
G="https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/services"
lig=requests.get(f"{G}/ligands",params={"name":"metformin"},timeout=60).json()
print(type(lig), lig if not isinstance(lig,list) else lig[:2])

import requests
q="""query D($id:String!){ drug(chemblId:$id){ id name drugType description maximumClinicalStage
 mechanismsOfAction{ rows{ mechanismOfAction actionType targetName targets{ id approvedSymbol approvedName } references{source ids} } }
 indications{ count rows{ disease{ id name } } } } }"""
r=requests.post("https://api.platform.opentargets.org/api/v4/graphql",
                json={"query":q,"variables":{"id":"CHEMBL1431"}},timeout=60).json()
print("errors:",r.get("errors"))
d=(r.get("data") or {}).get("drug")
if d:
    print(d["id"], d["name"], d["drugType"], "maxStage",d.get("maximumClinicalStage"))
    print("desc:",(d.get("description") or "")[:400])
    for m in d["mechanismsOfAction"]["rows"]:
        print(" MoA:",m["mechanismOfAction"],"|",m["actionType"],"| targetName",m.get("targetName"),
              "| targets",[(t["approvedSymbol"],t["id"]) for t in (m.get("targets") or [])],
              "| refs",m.get("references"))
    print(" indications count:",d["indications"]["count"])
    print("  ", [i["disease"]["name"] for i in d["indications"]["rows"][:20]])

content.text:
## Identity

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ChEMBL ID | **CHEMBL1431** (salt: CHEMBL1703, metformin hydrochloride) | ChEMBL REST `/molecule` |
| PubChem CID | **4091** | PubChem PUG-REST |
| SMILES / MW | `CN(C)C(=N)NC(=N)N` / 129.17 Da, AlogP −1.03 | ChEMBL |
| Status | max_phase 4, first approval **1995**; ATC **A10BA02**, biguanide | ChEMBL, KEGG D00944 |
| Approved indication | Adjunct to diet/exercise for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes, adults and children ≥10 y | openFDA label (eff. 2024-08-21) |

## Annotated molecular targets

ChEMBL's curated mechanism table and Open Targets (which ingests it) agree on exactly **two** inhibitory mechanisms, both mitochondrial:

1. **Mitochondrial complex I / NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase** — action type INHIBITOR. ChEMBL target `CHEMBL2363065`, a 50-subunit PROTEIN COMPLEX (MT-ND1–6, NDUFA/B/S/V families); Open Targets maps it to 50 Ensembl genes.
2. **Mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPD2)** — action type INHIBITOR. ChEMBL `CHEMBL3391681`, single protein **UniProt P43304**, Ensembl ENSG00000115159.

Both are supported by the same four references (PMIDs fetched from PubMed E-utilities): 24847880 (*Nature* 2014, Madiraju et al., mGPD inhibition suppresses gluconeogenesis), 25017630 (*Biochem J* 2014, biguanide effects on oxidative phosphorylation), 23277337 (*Trends Pharmacol Sci* 2013), 23358356 (*Nat Rev Endocrinol* 2013).

**KEGG disagrees** and annotates the target as **AMPK (PRKAA1/PRKAA2, HSA:5562 5563, KO:K07198)**, efficacy "AMP kinase activator," mapped to pathways hsa04152 (AMPK signaling), hsa04910 (insulin signaling), hsa04920 (adipocytokine signaling). This is the well-known indirect route: complex I inhibition raises AMP/ADP, activating AMPK via LKB1 — AMPK is a downstream effector, not a binding target. The two annotations are complementary rather than contradictory.

I could not query the Guide to PHARMACOLOGY: its web service now returns `"API key is missing"` and no key is configured in this environment.

## The quantitative bioactivity picture — metformin is a very weak ligand

I pulled all **3,110** ChEMBL activity records for CHEMBL1431 + CHEMBL1703 (assay types: 1,476 toxicity, 1,090 functional, 384 binding, 148 ADMET). Of these, **748** are dose-response values in nM (IC50/Ki/EC50/AC50/Kd):

- Median potency **22.2 mM**; 10th percentile 30 µM, 90th percentile 215 mM
- **92%** of values are weaker than 10 µM; **78%** are weaker than 1 mM
- Only **11 of 3,110** records carry a pChEMBL value at all, and the apparent "potent" ones are screening artifacts, not targets: Prelamin-A/C pChEMBL 8.46 (assay CHEMBL1614544, a qHTS counter-screen), MCF7 IC50 9.9 nM and PC-3 IC50 189 nM (assays CHEMBL4699781/2, single-report cell-growth outliers), HepG2 EC50 270 nM. Named receptors appear only at ≥5 µM — α1A-adrenergic AC50 5.6 µM (assay CHEMBL5291732), DPP-4 IC50 29 µM.

PubChem independently confirms the flat profile: of **2,691** assay records for CID 4091, **950 are Inactive, 1,554 Unspecified, 170 Inconclusive, and only 17 Active** — and none of the 17 has an annotated protein-gene target. They are cytotoxicity, Tox21/ToxCast, and pharmacokinetic entries (e.g. AID 1920329/1920330 are human CSF Cmax = 0.74 µM, not activity).

Pharmacologically this is consistent: metformin acts at the millimolar concentrations it reaches inside hepatocyte mitochondria after OCT1-mediated accumulation, not at nanomolar receptor occupancy. ChEMBL carries **SLC22A1 (OCT1)** values of 1.23–1.62 mM — transporter Km, i.e. metformin is a transport substrate; OCT1/OCT2/MATE1 govern its disposition rather than being efficacy targets.

## Breadth of investigation

Open Targets reports **247 indications** for CHEMBL1431 (its own description string says 93 approved and 209 investigational), spanning oncology (medulloblastoma, osteosarcoma, rectal and colon carcinoma, sarcoma), fertility/PCOS (infertility, female infertility), cardiometabolic (myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, diabetic retinopathy), and aging-adjacent indications (sarcopenia) — reflecting the very large repurposing literature rather than validated new targets.

Confidence: the target annotations and all numbers above are database lookups, not predictions. The one judgment call is my reading that the handful of sub-µM ChEMBL/PubChem values are artifacts — that is my interpretation of single-report outliers against a 748-point distribution centered at 22 mM, not a curated flag in the source.

## ANSWER

**Curated targets (ChEMBL CHEMBL1431 / Open Targets, 2 mechanisms, both INHIBITOR):**
1. Mitochondrial complex I, NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase — ChEMBL `CHEMBL2363065` (50-subunit complex)
2. Mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase **GPD2** — ChEMBL `CHEMBL3391681`, UniProt **P43304**
Refs: PMIDs 24847880, 25017630, 23277337, 23358356. **KEGG D00944** instead annotates **AMPK (PRKAA1/2, genes 5562/5563)** as the target ("AMP kinase activator") — the downstream effector, not a binding site.

**Bioactivity:** metformin is a very low-potency ligand. Across 748 dose-response records in ChEMBL, median = **22.2 mM**; 92% weaker than 10 µM, 78% weaker than 1 mM; only 11/3,110 records have a pChEMBL value. ## Annotated molecular targets

ChEMBL's curated mechanism table and Open Targets (which ingests it) agree on exactly **two** inhibitory mechanisms, both mitochondrial:

1. **Mitochondrial complex I / NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase** — action type INHIBITOR. ChEMBL target `CHEMBL2363065`, a 50-subunit PROTEIN COMPLEX (MT-ND1–6, NDUFA/B/S/V families); Open Targets maps it to 50 Ensembl genes.
2. **Mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPD2)** — action type INHIBITOR. ChEMBL `CHEMBL3391681`, single protein **UniProt P43304**, Ensembl ENSG00000115159.

Both are supported by the same four references (PMIDs fetched from PubMed E-utilities): 24847880 (*Nature* 2014, Madiraju et al., mGPD inhibition suppresses gluconeogenesis), 25017630 (*Biochem J* 2014, biguanide effects on oxidative phosphorylation), 23277337 (*Trends Pharmacol Sci* 2013), 23358356 (*Nat Rev Endocrinol* 2013).

**KEGG disagrees** and annotates the target as **AMPK (PRKAA1/PRKAA2, HSA:5562 5563, KO:K07198)**, efficacy "AMP kinase activator," mapped to pathways hsa04152 (AMPK signaling), hsa04910 (insulin signaling), hsa04920 (adipocytokine signaling). This is the well-known indirect route: complex I inhibition raises AMP/ADP, activating AMPK via LKB1 — AMPK is a downstream effector, not a binding target. The two annotations are complementary rather than contradictory.

## The quantitative bioactivity picture — metformin is a very weak ligand

I pulled all **3,110** ChEMBL activity records for CHEMBL1431 + CHEMBL1703 (assay types: 1,476 toxicity, 1,090 functional, 384 binding, 148 ADMET). Of these, **748** are dose-response values in nM (IC50/Ki/EC50/AC50/Kd):

- Median potency **22.2 mM**; 10th percentile 30 µM, 90th percentile 215 mM
- **92%** of values are weaker than 10 µM; **78%** are weaker than 1 mM
- Only **11 of 3,110** records carry a pChEMBL value at all, and the apparent "potent" ones are screening artifacts, not targets: Prelamin-A/C pChEMBL 8.46 (assay CHEMBL1614544, a qHTS counter-screen), MCF7 IC50 9.9 nM and PC-3 IC50 189 nM (assays CHEMBL4699781/2, single-report cell-growth outliers), HepG2 EC50 270 nM. Named receptors appear only at ≥5 µM — α1A-adrenergic AC50 5.6 µM (assay CHEMBL5291732), DPP-4 IC50 29 µM.

PubChem independently confirms the flat profile: of **2,691** assay records for CID 4091, **950 are Inactive, 1,554 Unspecified, 170 Inconclusive, and only 17 Active** — and none of the 17 has an annotated protein-gene target. They are cytotoxicity, Tox21/ToxCast, and pharmacokinetic entries (e.g. AID 1920329/1920330 are human CSF Cmax = 0.74 µM, not activity).

Pharmacologically this is consistent: metformin acts at the millimolar concentrations it reaches inside hepatocyte mitochondria after OCT1-mediated accumulation, not at nanomolar receptor occupancy. ChEMBL carries **SLC22A1 (OCT1)** values of 1.23–1.62 mM — transporter Km, i.e. metformin is a transport substrate; OCT1/OCT2/MATE1 govern its disposition rather than being efficacy targets.

## Breadth of investigation

Open Targets reports **247 indications** for CHEMBL1431 (its own description string says 93 approved and 209 investigational), spanning oncology (medulloblastoma, osteosarcoma, rectal and colon carcinoma, sarcoma), fertility/PCOS (infertility, female infertility), cardiometabolic (myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, diabetic retinopathy), and aging-adjacent indications (sarcopenia) — reflecting the very large repurposing literature rather than validated new targets.

Confidence: the target annotations and all numbers above are database lookups, not predictions. The one judgment call is my reading that the handful of sub-µM ChEMBL/PubChem values are artifacts — that is my interpretation of single-report outliers against a 748-point distribution centered at 22 mM, not a curated flag in the source.
